subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a scoped trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should that live as a shared approval/elevated/tool-class policy instead of a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: Source inspection shows the mode is absent, but deciding when a channel sender may skip approval prompts changes a security boundary and config surface that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared policy with explicit sender, group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics.

options.title: Keep existing approval model
options.body: Decline the bypass and document that operators who want no prompts should use the existing elevated/full and host-policy posture deliberately.

options.title: Add Telegram-only shortcut
options.body: Implement the requested Telegram config directly, accepting narrower scope but higher risk of policy drift from shared approvals.

recommendation.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared policy with explicit sender, group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily product/security policy and config-surface direction, with Telegram and approval owners needed after the boundary is chosen.
